title: Neuromodulation of Executive Control for Substance Use Disorders
summary: The purpose of this research study is to determine the effectiveness of a procedure called transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) using a device called StarStim cap and its effects on drug cravings.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Able to provide written consent and comply with study procedures.
2. Adults aged 18 to 65 years at the time of consent.
3. Meets the MINI diagnostic criteria for either methamphetamine use disorder (MUD).

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Any contraindications for tACS or MRI scanning (tACS contraindication: history of seizures; potential MRI contraindications, up to the discretion of AIRC and CBH staff: metal implants, pacemakers or any other implanted electrical device, injury with metal, braces, dental implants, non-removable body piercings, pregnancy, breathing or moving disorder).
2. Any medical condition or treatment with neurological sequelae (i.e., stroke, tumor).
3. Over 9 months of abstinence from substance use.
4. A head injury resulting in a loss of consciousness exceeding 30 minutes (i.e., moderate or severe TBI).
5. Presence of a condition that would render study measures difficult or impossible to administer or interpret.
6. Entrance to the treatment program under a court mandate. (i.e. legally incarcerated).
7. History of ECT or cortical energy exposure within the past 6 months, including participation in any other neuromodulation studies.
sponsor: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
